title: Integral pushforward identifies a base-change arrow with the pasted arrow
statement:
Let $f':X'\to S'$ and $\pi:S''\to S'$ be morphisms of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with $\pi$ integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Form $X''=X'\times_{S'}S''$, with projections $\pi':X''\to X'$ and $f'':X''\to S''$ [sbc-def-base-change-square]. Let $g':T\to S''$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, set $Y=X''\times_{S''}T$, and let $h':Y\to X''$, $e:Y\to T$ be its projections. Set $g=\pi\circ g'$ and $h=\pi'\circ h'$. Let $q\geq0$ and $F$ be an abelian etale sheaf on $T$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. For higher direct images and inverse images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], there are natural isomorphisms
$$\pi'_* (f'')^{-1}R^qg'_*F\cong(f')^{-1}R^qg_*F,\qquad
\pi'_*R^qh'_*e^{-1}F\cong R^qh_*e^{-1}F.$$
Under these isomorphisms $\pi'_*(\operatorname{BC}^q_{f'',g'}(F))$ equals $\operatorname{BC}^q_{f',g}(F)$ [sbc-def-base-change-map]. Thus if the former base-change arrow over $S''$ is an isomorphism, the pasted base-change arrow over $S'$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-integral-morphism-base-change] to the Cartesian square with integral vertical map $\pi:S''\to S'$ and base map $f':X'\to S'$. Its base change $\pi'$ is integral. By [sbc-lem-integral-etale-direct-image-exact], both $\pi_*$ and $\pi'_*$ are exact on abelian etale sheaves and their bounded-below derived functors are their termwise functors. Also $(f')^{-1}$ and $(f'')^{-1}$ are exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact].

proof.text: Use [lem-sbc-integral-underived-exchange] with coefficient ring $\mathbf Z$, $(f,f',g,g')=(\pi,\pi',f',f'')$. This gives the canonical exchange isomorphism $E:(f')^{-1}\pi_*\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi'_*(f'')^{-1}$ on abelian sheaves. Apply it termwise: naturality makes $E$ commute with every differential. All four functors are exact by step 1, so [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor](2) identifies their bounded-below derived functors with the termwise functors. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] descends this termwise natural isomorphism to $D^+$. To identify it with the canonical derived exchange, apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-termwise](a),(b): choose a bounded below K-injective resolution $K\xrightarrow{\sim}QI$ and a K-injective resolution $j:(f'')^{-1}I\to J$. With the source and target comparison isomorphisms specified there, the derived exchange is the class of $\pi'_*(j)\circ E_I$. Exactness of $\pi'_*$ from step 1 implies that $\pi'_*(j)$ is a quasi-isomorphism, since the natural cohomology comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] identifies its cohomology maps with $\pi'_*H^r(j)$. Under the exact-functor comparisons, naturality of the descended $E$ with respect to the resolution maps identifies this class with its component at $K$. Thus it is exactly the canonical derived exchange, and is an isomorphism. Thus $E_K:(f')^{-1}R\pi_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\pi'_*(f'')^{-1}K$ for every $K\in D^+(S''_{\mathrm{Et}})$.

proof.text:
Set $K=Rg'_*F[0]$. Let $A:(f')^{-1}Rg_*F[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}(f')^{-1}R\pi_*Rg'_*F[0]$ and $B:Rh_*e^{-1}F[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}R\pi'_*Rh'_*e^{-1}F[0]$ be the composition comparisons of [def-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-composition], using $g=\pi\circ g'$ and $h=\pi'\circ h'$. Apply clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-identity-pasting] to the two squares, with $(f,f',g,g')=(\pi,\pi',f',f'')$ and $(e,e',g'')=(g',h',e)$. By [sbc-def-base-change-map] the exchange on this exchanged square is precisely the specified base-change map. The pasting identity is therefore
$$B\circ\operatorname{BC}_{f',g}(F[0])=R\pi'_*\bigl(\operatorname{BC}_{f'',g'}(F[0])\bigr)\circ E_K\circ A.$$
This records the arrow itself, with the comparison maps inserted, rather than just identifying its endpoints.

proof.text:
For an exact functor $P$, [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] identifies $H^q(PC)$ with $P(H^qC)$ naturally: $P$ preserves the kernel of $d^q$, the image of $d^{q-1}$, and their quotient. These comparisons descend to $D^+$ because cohomology inverts quasi-isomorphisms and their naturality holds on maps of complexes, hence also on inverses of quasi-isomorphisms. Apply them to the exact functors $\pi_*,\pi'_*,(f')^{-1},(f'')^{-1}$ from step 1. With the higher-image convention of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and the degreewise map of [sbc-def-base-change-map], $H^q(E_K\circ A)$ is a natural isomorphism
$C:(f')^{-1}R^qg_*F\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi'_*(f'')^{-1}R^qg'_*F$,
and $H^q(B)$ is a natural isomorphism
$D:R^qh_*e^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi'_*R^qh'_*e^{-1}F$.
Their inverses are the two isomorphisms in the statement.

proof.text:
Apply $H^q$ to the equality in step 3. The naturality of the cohomology comparisons used in step 4 gives exactly
$$D\circ\operatorname{BC}^q_{f',g}(F)=\pi'_*\bigl(\operatorname{BC}^q_{f'',g'}(F)\bigr)\circ C.$$
Multiplying by $D^{-1}$ and $C^{-1}$ identifies the pushed-forward arrow with the pasted arrow under the stated isomorphisms. If $b=\operatorname{BC}^q_{f'',g'}(F)$ has inverse $b^{-1}$, then $\pi'_*(b)$ has inverse $\pi'_*(b^{-1})$, since a functor preserves identities and composition. Consequently the pasted arrow $D^{-1}\pi'_*(b)C$ has inverse $C^{-1}\pi'_*(b^{-1})D$. This proves the final implication.
